claims: "Integrity" is the name of the Orion spacecraft capsule for the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis II mission successfully completed a 10-day crewed lunar flyby in April 2026.
Reid Wiseman, Christina Koch, Victor Glover, and Jeremy Hansen were the crew of the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis II crew completed the mission.
The Artemis II crew splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
During the Artemis II mission, the crew conducted proximity operations.
During the Artemis II mission, the crew maneuvered near the ICPS stage.
During the Artemis II mission, the crew broke the Apollo 13 distance record.
Integrity safely endured a high-speed reentry through Earth's atmosphere.
The high-speed reentry through Earth's atmosphere was considered the most dangerous part of the mission.
The Artemis II mission brought humans back to the vicinity of the Moon for the first time in over 50 years.
